doc.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025

title: Playing for singers and different keys
summary: Different keys are easy on bass because of finger patterns, though he has misled singers.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Did you have sort of an alarming moment the first time you played gigs with a girl singer, a woman singer, to find out that a lot of those tunes that you already knew were like a fourth or fifth away. Was that an issue?

Yeah sometimes. But most of the time on bass it’s not a big problem because of the way the bass is set up. It’s just basically playing the same finger patterns but moving your hand to a different area. It’s not like you have to play the black keys or you know, whatever they go through – madness with saxophones and trumpet you know. So it’s just basically playing the same lick but sliding on the neck to a different place you know. So it’s easier for us. Yeah.
But you have to play the right note. I’ve screwed some singers up.
